NPS Museum Handbook Part I, Chapter 4: Museum Collections Environment (2016)
https://www.nps.gov/subjects/museums/upload/MHI_Ch4_Environment.pdf
Publisher: US National Park Service
Sections: Museum Handbook I, Ch.4 §J.1–3, printed pp.4:46–4:49; PDF pp.49–52; Museum Handbook I, Ch.4 §§G.4/H.1, printed pp.4:30–4:32; PDF pp.33–35
Rights: US government NPS text generally public domain under 17 USC 105, unless otherwise indicated; third-party images excluded.
Change notice: selected excerpts; whitespace normalized. See THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt and licenses/.
if temperature and RH levels are stable and within the recommended set point and permissible range
Assemble a qualified team to carefully plan and implement a climate control strategy.
Implement non-mechanical measures to control climate when and wherever feasible
Monitor regularly to insure that these controls are effective and adjust accordingly.
gather baseline and ongoing lighting information
Lower light intensity and duration in exhibit and storage areas.
Monitor and document light levels before and after taking any action to be sure that your changes have been effective.
be sure that light levels are at required levels and that UV blocking materials are still effective, that there is no IR and that visible light is appropriately controlled
